chapter: Joining Goodman and views on arranging
title: Weekly quotas and why he left Goodman
summary: He had to write a number of charts weekly and left because he could not hear any more.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: It's funny, when I played the recordings of things you wrote for Goodman, the contrast for me for things like "Superman" or "Clarinet A La King"

I just get the sense--you can get a sense of what you were really involved in, what was really interesting to you and what, on the other sand you were just doing because somebody said, here is a pop tune that we need to play, do a chart on it.
I had to do a certain number every week.
If you didn't do things a certain way--there were certain things that Benny wouldn't accept. He didn't say don't do it, but he simply wouldn't play

it. So why knock yourself out on something that he's not going to use. I remember why I left Benny. I left Benny because I couldn't hear anymore. I couldn't hear G or C. In order to do what I was doing, there was just too much repeti- tion and I needed stimulation of another sort at that time.
